messages.author: 531698ef6aa88c88
messages.subject: Multi-session closed population models
parts:
Hello all,

I'm cross posting this question that I also posted to the Spatial-Capture-Recapture group in hopes of casting a broader net of responses so I apologize to anyone who gets this twice.  Thanks.

"Hello all,
I'm asking this question here because it relates to a multi-session closed population capture-recapture design presented in the SCR book.  For my case, I'm interested in the relationship between habitat covariates and abundance over multiple study areas.  However, study area size varied at a magnitude that it certainly contributes to variation in abundance.  To account for area, I specified a log-linear model similar to that which was provided in Panel 14.1 in the SCR book except that it know includes a deterministic offset term.  To test my code, I simulated closed CMR data for each study area with p = 0.3 and number of occasions set at 10.  Results for the intercept and "habitat" coefficient of the log-linear model were spot on.  However, the estimates for study area-specific lambda were consistently, but only slightly, underestimated and precisely so which resulted in credible intervals rarely containing the true value.  Additionally, p was substantially overestimated at 0.4.  Has anyone run into this situation before?  I don't think it is a model-specification problem, but I can post my code just in case.  It almost seems like this is a situation where some model parameters are only weakly identifiable when linking multiple parametric models based on the same data.  I welcome any ideas or insights.

Cheers
Jared"

messages.subject: Re: Multi-session closed population models
parts:
Update:

After some exchanges on the SCR google group, I found the problem and corresponding solution.  It turned out to be a coding error so consider this topic resolved.

Cheers
Jared
